articles.title: Evaluation of Acid Production as a Metabolic Phenotype in Cutibacterium acnes Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint Infections.
articles.authors: Frappa N, Listopadzki TR, Lutnick E, Feng L, Crane JK, Duquin TR
articles.population: Clinical isolates of Cutibacterium acnes from shoulder periprosthetic joint infections
articles.outcomes: Acid production (change in pH) and bacterial growth (optical density) at 72 hours; diagnostic discrimination for definite infection
articles.take_home: Clindamycin-resistant C. acnes produced less acid than susceptible strains, but acid production alone was only modestly useful at distinguishing definite infections from other cases. The study suggests metabolic testing might help in future research but is not yet ready for clinical use on its own.

articles.title: Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty with the Tornier Perform Posterior Augmented Glenoid versus Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty for the Treatment of Walch B2 and B3 Glenoids: A Propensity Score Matched Analysis.
articles.authors: Harkin W, Shen A, Hussain ZB, Hyeamang LJ, Kurowicki J, Lew R, et al.
articles.population: Adults with glenohumeral osteoarthritis and Walch B2 or B3 posterior glenoid deficiency with intact rotator cuff
articles.sample_size: 208 shoulders (98 anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty, 110 reverse total shoulder arthroplasty); 72 after propensity matching
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (ASES, SANE, VAS pain), range of motion, revision rates, radiolucency
articles.take_home: Both types of shoulder replacement surgery produced excellent results at two years with similar pain relief and function scores. Anatomic replacement offered better arm movement, whilst reverse replacement showed fewer imaging changes on X-ray.

articles.title: Cortical Button and Suture Anchor Fixation for Distal Biceps Tendon Repair Provide Similar Clinical Outcomes and Complication Profiles: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Nadeem SM, Yousafzai H, Haque O, Bouchard MD, Vivekanantha P, Parlange A, et al.
articles.population: Adults with distal biceps tendon rupture treated surgically
articles.sample_size: 1,757 patients across 10 comparative studies (693 cortical button, 490 cortical button plus interference screw, 574 suture anchors)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (DASH, QuickDASH, MEPS, EQ-5D-5L), range of motion, strength recovery, and complications including re-rupture and nerve injuries
articles.take_home: Both cortical button and suture anchor fixation methods produce similar good results after distal biceps tendon repair, with patients recovering near-full elbow movement and about 85-95% of normal strength. Neither method shows clear superiority, though nerve-related complications (mainly temporary nerve irritation) occur in both groups at similar rates.

articles.title: Locking Plate Fixation with Cemented Screws versus Delta Xtend Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty for Complex Proximal Humerus Fractures in the Elderly: A Matched-Pair Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Martinez-Catalan N, Garcia-Rubio C, Valencia M, Luengo-Alonso G, Delgado C, Calvo E, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged over 65 years with complex proximal humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, Constant Score, pain, quality of life, complication rates, and revision surgery rates
articles.take_home: Both cemented locking plate fixation and reverse shoulder replacement gave good results in elderly patients with complex shoulder fractures. Locking plates preserved better rotation of the shoulder, but both treatments had similar pain relief, overall function, and rates of complications or further surgery.

articles.title: Spin in Systematic Reviews on Patch-Augmented Rotator Cuff Repair: Prevalence, Predictors, and Methodological Implications.
articles.authors: Al-Badaineh M, Josan H, Imran B, Ebeid I, Mekhail J, Abdou M, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
articles.population: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses comparing patch-augmented versus non-augmented rotator cuff repair
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of spin in abstracts, types of spin identified, associations with funding status, methodological quality and journal impact factor
articles.take_home: Most abstracts (81%) of systematic reviews on shoulder patch repair contained spin or misleading presentation of results, linked to poor methodological quality rather than funding or journal prestige. Readers should carefully check the full study details before trusting abstract conclusions.

articles.title: Metabolic Bone Disease Care Practice Patterns and the Correlation Between Computed Tomography and Fracture Risk Assessment Tool Score in Patients Undergoing Total Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Wang Z, King J, Prentice A, Aibinder W
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing primary total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Metabolic bone disease screening and treatment rates, correlation between CT Hounsfield unit measurements and fracture risk assessment scores, comparison of bone density between high-risk and low-risk patients
articles.take_home: Many patients at high risk of fractures before shoulder replacement surgery are not being screened or treated for bone disease, with only 50% receiving bone density scans and 13% receiving osteoporosis medication. Patients at higher risk had significantly weaker bones on CT scans, highlighting opportunities to improve bone health care around the time of surgery.

articles.title: Posterior Translation of the Humeral Head after Arthroscopic Bankart Repair: A Quantitative Analysis of Preoperative and Postoperative Axial MRI.
articles.authors: So SP, Seok HG, Jeon IH
articles.population: Patients with anterior shoulder instability undergoing arthroscopic Bankart repair
articles.outcomes: Humeral head anteroposterior translation measured on axial MRI before and after surgery; preoperative translation increased from 0.59 mm to 1.50 mm postoperatively (mean change 0.91 mm)
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic Bankart repair surgery significantly reduces how far the upper arm bone moves forward in the shoulder socket in patients with instability. Patients who had longer-standing instability before surgery showed greater improvements in humeral head positioning after repair.

articles.title: Anatomical versus reverse total shoulder arthroplasty for primary glenohumeral osteoarthritis with an intact rotator cuff : a systematic review.
articles.authors: Shah PP, Jayawardena R, Wong R, Poff C, Maassen NH, Shi L
articles.population: Patients with glenohumeral osteoarthritis and an intact rotator cuff
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, patient-reported outcomes, complications, revisions, cost, radiological changes, and satisfaction
articles.take_home: Anatomical and reverse total shoulder replacements produce similar results in patients with osteoarthritis and an intact rotator cuff. Anatomical replacement may give slightly better movement, but both procedures work well and reverse replacement is a reasonable alternative.

articles.title: Clinical practice on treatment of primary traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation: a multidisciplinary guideline.
articles.authors: Van Gastel ML, Hekman KMC, Boon F, Nelen SD, Schep NWL, Van der Meijden OAJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients with primary traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation
articles.outcomes: Optimal diagnosis and management pathway covering reduction technique, pain management, immobilisation, physical therapy, risk factors for recurrence, and surgical decision-making
articles.take_home: Primary shoulder dislocations need prompt treatment with imaging, and management should follow a structured pathway including careful reduction, brief immobilisation, and early physiotherapy. Young patients, males, and athletes have higher risk of the shoulder dislocating again and may benefit from surgery.

articles.title: Outcomes of primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty in patients younger than 65 years: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Johri M, Bouzid NM, Thibeault JW, Yazdanpanah S, Reiter CR, Setliff JC, et al.
articles.population: Patients under 65 years undergoing primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 13 studies included; weighted mean age 55.4 years, 60.9% female
articles.outcomes: Range of motion (forward flexion, external rotation, abduction, internal rotation), patient-reported outcome measures (ASES, VAS pain, Constant-Murley, SST, SPADI, UCLA), complication rate 13%, revision rate 8%
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder replacement in younger patients (under 65) improves movement and function, with pain reducing to 2.6 out of 10. About 1 in 8 patients experience complications and 1 in 12 need further surgery, mainly for shoulder instability.
